name: fresh-harness
description: The harness, installable — and the repo, fresh

spec.why: The harness must ship as a product: agents and skills packaged under treadle/harness behind an interactive installer (treadle init harness) like speckkit's specify CLI. The repo must read as new: no dead engine links in live surfaces.

requirements.text: agents/ and skills/ live under treadle/harness/ with a versioned manifest (harness/0.1) describing components, surfaces, transforms, and hooks (empty = honestly unsupported).
The installer compiles manifest + choices into an explicit plan (component, surface, source, destination, transform, mode); --dry-run prints it; --json emits it.

Apply writes exactly the plan: idempotency by content hash AFTER normalization (LF line endings + exactly one trailing newline), so platform checkout differences never flap modes; --force overwrites; never deletes unknown files; .gitattributes pins eol=lf repo-wide.
Flags are complete: --agent --scope --skills --no-agents --no-hooks --yes; no TTY without required flags exits 2 with the exact remediation command.
The engine (plan compiler + apply) is fully unit-tested through flags; no logic lives above the flag layer.
The interactive skin renders agent/scope/component choices and returns flags only; thin by construction and asserted.
Surface adapters: pi project+user, claude project+global, codex user (project verified), copilot project-only — paths verified at build; failures refuse, never guess.

Hooks ship as JS payload files (harness/hooks/<id>.js) described by manifest rows carrying file + per-surface wiring (pi: extension file to .pi/extensions/; claude: settings.json matcher/command invoking the JS; codex: config notify invoking the JS; copilot: null — no hooks or extensions, printed honestly). T-3 authors the first real hook payload and its wiring.

Copilot is a full adapter: .github/copilot-instructions.md + .github/agents/*.md (frontmatter) + .github/skills/<n>/SKILL.md (Agent Skills format, identity transform); every path verified against live docs at build; refusals over guesses (Q-3).
engine/ and graphify-out/ residue deleted; .gitignore prevents return.

ci.yml runs from the repo root: defaults.run.working-directory: treadle for run steps AND cache-dependency-path: treadle/pnpm-lock.yaml on setup-node (defaults do not reach uses: steps); FR-11 evidence = one full green matrix run post-push, recorded.
A links gate (scripts/link-check.mjs + pnpm links) walks live surfaces and fails on any unresolved markdown link; archive excluded by design.
The wiki tells the TS truth: treadle.md and sdd-harness-architecture.md rewritten; retired engine pages superseded per Q-4; zero engine/(okf|loom) links in live surfaces.
The know ritual ends green: validate 0/0, fingerprints + stamp updated, anchors 0, status fresh.

Dogfood-first: manifest rows carry explicit destination paths; the installer lands content in project .pi/{skills,agents,extensions} and .codex/{skills,agents} in this repo; T-0 pre-cleans the known legacy drift (.pi/agents/red-forman.md typo copy, stale .pi/skills/build-kb resources) so convergence is achievable; the plan lists unmanaged leftovers and --force removes exactly the confirmed list; what passes evaluation — hooks and extensions included — is promoted back into the harness; recorded as evidence.
The wave closes through its own loop: every task evidence-recorded, review rounds in the verdicts, corpus byte-stable, closed by human:owner.
Reversibility: every apply records its plan to a state file listing exactly what was written; `init harness --remove` deletes exactly those paths and nothing else.

clarifications.question: Hooks v1 policy: ship hooks only where a surface natively supports them (Claude Code settings.json, Codex config notify), and print an honest 'not supported' for pi and Copilot?
options: hooks as JS files everywhere: pi extensions (.pi/extensions), claude settings wiring, codex notify — copilot honestly none
clarifications.answer: hooks as JS files everywhere: pi extensions (.pi/extensions), claude settings wiring, codex notify — copilot honestly none

clarifications.question: The interactive layer: add @clack/prompts (small MIT lib, the speckkit-grade UX) or build a zero-dependency arrow-key selector we own (~150 lines)?
GitHub Copilot v1: install as copilot-instructions.md + prompt files (.github/prompts), no agents (cloud-only) and no global?
options: full copilot: custom instructions + agents + skills (all supported per owner; verified in research)
clarifications.answer: full copilot: custom instructions + agents + skills (all supported per owner; verified in research)

clarifications.question: Retired wiki pages (systems/okf-engine.md, loom-engine.md): supersede into docs/archive and delete from the live wiki, or keep in place with SUPERSEDED banners?
Global installs v1: pi to ~/.pi/agent, claude to ~/.claude, codex to ~/.codex (Copilot none) — with an explicit confirm that shows absolute paths before any write outside the repo?
options: dogfood-first: project .pi + .codex in this repo, promotion into harness; globals later
clarifications.answer: dogfood-first: project .pi + .codex in this repo, promotion into harness; globals later

out_of_scope: new-project and roadmap skills stay stubs
pack birth stays do init (no treadle init spec this wave)
copilot org-level agents, pi extensions, remote installs

decisions.because: The owner asked for the package; one repo one truth; per-surface npm packages are sprawl we refuse (engram-dev split is a later recorded wave). Root noise dies.

decisions.decision: Plan-then-apply: an inspectable plan precedes every write; refuse is defined (destination holds foreign content without --force; apply exits 3 listing the row)
decisions.because: No write before review; the plan is testable output, apply is deterministic replay; copy-as-you-go is unreviewable.

decisions.decision: Flags are the engine; the interactive layer is skin that only produces flags
decisions.because: TUIs test badly; engines test well. Every choice has a flag; no TTY + no flags = exit 2 with the remediation command.

decisions.decision: Adapters are manifest rows plus two tiny transforms (identity; skill-to-prompt)
decisions.because: A new surface is a manifest row; a new transform is one registry function. Per-surface script directories are the sprawl we came to escape.

decisions.decision: Hooks ship as JS files wired per surface (pi extensions, claude settings wiring, codex notify); copilot prints the honest no
decisions.because: Owner answer Q-1: pi has extensions (local-documented), copilot has neither hooks nor extensions; JS files are the one medium all three can invoke; a printed no beats an emulated lie.

decisions.decision: Idempotency by normalized content hash (LF + one trailing newline; .gitattributes pins eol=lf); never delete unknown files; applied plans recorded for --remove
decisions.because: Destinations are shared (.claude/, ~/.codex); a mirror would destroy foreign content. Re-run = same; --force is explicit.

decisions.decision: Dogfood-first: project .pi and .codex in this repo; promotion into the harness; globals later
decisions.because: Owner answer Q-5: the named targets are .pi/{agents,skills} and .codex/{agents,skills}; evaluation happens in real work; what passes — hooks/extensions included — is promoted. The absolute-path confirm stays recorded for the later global wave.

decisions.decision: The cleanup is checked, not vibes: links gate + know ritual prove freshness
decisions.because: Manual sweeps rot back. The gate runs in CI; the archive stays untouched because history is evidence (Q-4 default: supersede into docs/archive).

decisions.decision: Copilot is a full adapter: custom instructions + agents + skills (Agent Skills format); no hooks
decisions.because: Owner answer Q-3 corrects my cloud-only claim: latest Copilot supports all three. Paths verified against live docs at T-3; refusals over guesses. The earlier prompt-file conversion design is superseded.

decisions.decision: Reversibility: every apply records its write list; --remove deletes exactly it
decisions.because: R1 DEFECT 9: an installer product with no reversal contradicts the pack reversibility posture; the state file is the contract between apply and remove.
